The main takeaway from our work is that

stress exposure sets in motion a process of adaptation that unfolds over time, that the process is modified by both structural and personal factors, and that it can only be understood by using longitudinal methods and by conducting experimental interventions.
social factors in the form of social support and coping processes play a critical role in moderating the impact of stress on health outcomes.
social factors in psychosocial stress, and the processes by which they are linked to health, are complex.
